notes.1i: Many candidates correctly described the trend shown in Fig. 1.4 by stating that as the pH increased the percentage mass of the protein remaining increased.
notes.1ii: Many candidates correctly explained that between pH2 and pH6 the activity of the pepsin gradually declined. They correctly suggested that, as a result of the active site changing shape, the substrate could no longer bind to the active site resulting in fewer enzyme-substrate complexes forming. Many candidates correctly suggested that the enzyme had become denatured. The most common error was to give a description of the graph rather than give an explanation of what was occurring to the pepsin as the pH increased.
notes.1iii: Most candidates correctly recorded a result for X using one of the symbols in the key.
notes.1iv: Some candidates correctly estimated the concentration of protein in X from their results based on the fact that 100% M contained 12g of protein in 100cm3.
notes.1v: Most candidates correctly stated that a significant source of error was the difficulty of judging the exact shade of colour.
notes.1vi: The majority of candidates were able to suggest three improvements to the investigation so that a more accurate estimate of the concentration of protein in X could be obtained. Many candidates correctly suggested preparing more concentrations of milk close to the estimate for X with narrower intervals between each concentration. Some candidates correctly suggested using a colorimeter and using the data to draw a graph. notes.2i: The majority of candidates gained credit for measuring the scale bar and the line Z within an acceptable range. Many candidates measured the scale bar in millimeters and showed this figure multiplied by 1000 to convert into micrometres before dividing by 317. Many candidates correctly calculated the magnification of Fig. 2.1 in this way then divided their measurement for Z by this magnification to calculate the actual width of the root and used the correct units.
notes.2ii: The stronger candidates organised the table into three columns, with one column for features, one headed K1 and one headed Fig. 2.1. Many candidates listed at least three observable differences between K1 and Fig. 2.1 such as K1 had fewer layers of tissues than Fig. 2.1, K1 had a smooth, continuous outer layer while Fig. 2.1 had a rough discontinuous outer layer and cells of K1 were larger than the cells of Fig. 2.1.
notes.key_messages: Candidates should use biological terms accurately. For example, in Question 1(a), the secondary structure of antibodies can be described as having beta or β-pleated sheets, not B-pleated sheets and, in Question 1(b)(ii), B-lymphocytes or B cells should be stated, rather than β cells. When quoting extracted data from graphs, candidates are reminded to refer to both axes in their answers. In Question 3(a)(ii), many often omitted the time. In addition, it was better to refer to a specific time from the x-axis rather than to state ‘at the end’.
notes.general_comments: General comments The paper differentiated well. Comments on specific questions The majority of candidates answered correctly, with only the weakest candidates finding it difficult. Questions 2, 4, 6, 16, 19, 23, 30, 34, 37 and 38 Almost all candidates found these questions straightforward and answered correctly. Some candidates found this question difficult. Only the stronger candidates were aware that microtubules carried out all three of the listed functions.
